steps.say: Stomach cancer comes in two very different forms. One grows as a lump in the lower stomach in older patients with chronic infection. The other soaks the whole wall with tiny cells, turns the stomach rigid, and runs in families with a faulty gene.
steps.tx: Intestinal-type distal tumours follow Helicobacter, smoking and salted foods, while diffuse **linitis plastica** (rigid leather-bottle stomach) with **signet ring** (mucin-filled ring cells) histology links to germline **CDH1** (cell adhesion gene) mutation, needing prophylactic total gastrectomy in carriers identified by family screening.

vis.alt: Illustration of a rigid thick-walled stomach beside a microscopic view of pale rounded tumour cells.
vis.caption: Diffuse gastric cancer: linitis plastica stomach with thickened wall and signet-ring cells from E-cadherin loss. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Scans miss tiny seedlings floating in the belly. Before committing to a big curative operation, the surgeon looks inside with a camera and washes the cavity. Cancer cells in that fluid mean the disease has already spread.
steps.tx: **Staging laparoscopy** (keyhole look inside the belly) with **peritoneal cytology** (microscopy of wash fluid) precedes surgery for **T3** (through-wall), **T4** (into nearby organs) or node-positive disease, because positive washings upstage the patient to metastatic **M1** (distant spread) disease and cancel a futile major resection.

steps.say: The extent of stomach removal follows the tumour's address. A low tumour leaves the upper stomach behind, while a high or junctional one takes the whole organ. In both cases the lymph glands around the great vessels come out in one packet.
steps.tx: Distal tumours take subtotal gastrectomy with a **5 cm** (five centimetre) proximal margin, while proximal disease takes total gastrectomy with **oesophagojejunostomy** (gullet-to-bowel join). **D2 dissection** (extended nodal clearance) harvests at least **16 nodes** (sixteen glands) for accurate staging and lasting cure.

steps.say: Surgery alone cures fewer than half of advanced cases, so drug treatment now brackets the operation. Strong patients receive multiple drugs before and after, and the response on repeat scans decides whether surgery still makes sense.
steps.tx: Perioperative **FLOT** (four-drug stomach regimen) as **perioperative chemotherapy** (drugs around surgery) improves survival in resectable **T2** (muscle-invasive) or higher disease, and adjuvant **S-1** (oral fluoropyrimidine) or capecitabine with oxaliplatin follows D2 resection in Asian protocols for fit patients. Restaging after chemotherapy confirms the tumour still suits resection.

steps.say: Not every stomach lump is adenocarcinoma. The stromal tumour grows from the gut's pacemaker cells and spreads through blood rather than lymph. Small ones are simply scooped out with a rim of normal wall, and glands are left alone.
steps.tx: Gastric **GIST** (stromal pacemaker tumour) under **2 cm** (two centimetres) without high-risk features needs **wedge resection** (local scoop excision) with **1 to 2 cm** (one to two centimetre) margins, skipping lymphadenectomy since nodal spread is rare in this disease and long-term cure follows.

vis.alt: Illustration of multiple rounded stomach and bowel tumours with a microscopic view of stained spindle cells.
vis.caption: GIST: multiple gastric and small bowel nodules arising from interstitial cells of Cajal with KIT staining. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Under the microscope these tumours carry a driver mutation that decides the drug. The common variant melts with one tablet a day, while a rare variant ignores it and needs a different agent. Testing comes before prescribing.
steps.tx: **KIT** (growth receptor gene) **exon 11** (segment eleven) mutation predicts imatinib response, and high-risk disease over **5 cm** (five centimetres) or over 5 mitoses takes adjuvant **imatinib** (targeted tablet) **400 mg** (four hundred milligrams) daily for 3 years. **PDGFRA** (related receptor gene) **D842V** (resistant variant) needs avapritinib instead.

steps.say: The stomach's lymphoid tumour usually surrenders to antibiotics alone when the triggering germ is present. Clearing the infection cures most early cases. Deep invasion or a stubborn genetic marker means stronger therapy is required.
steps.tx: Gastric **MALT lymphoma** (mucosal lymphoid tumour) with Helicobacter positivity regresses with **eradication** (germ clearance) alone in **80 percent** (eighty percent) of cases. Deep invasion or **t(11;18)** (resistant translocation) needs radiotherapy or rituximab-based therapy instead of any operation in most centres today.

steps.say: When cancer has seeded the whole cavity, the examination itself tells the story. Both ovaries enlarge, the belly button hardens, and a rectal shelf is felt. At this stage the surgeon aims to relieve blockage, not to cure.
steps.tx: **Krukenberg** (ovarian seeding) tumours fill both ovaries, the **Sister Mary Joseph** (umbilical) nodule hardens the navel, and a **Blumer shelf** (pelvic drop deposit) is felt rectally on examination. These transcoelomic signs mark palliation, with bypass or stenting for malignant obstruction to relieve symptoms.
